text:
maya: Heads-up — after the merge for rt-scheduler-reshuffle we're seeing a ~35% tokens/sec drop on our continuous-batcher fleet in prod. P95 queueing and tail latency climbed.
liam: ugh, which hosts/region? any correlation with kernel fallback logs?
maya: us-east-1 ctb nodes mostly. quick numbers: 
```
prod-ctb-us-east-1a: tokens/sec 120k -> 78k (post-merge)
P95 queue time: 250ms -> 420ms
avg batch size: 4.1 -> 2.3
KV cache hitrate: 0.82 -> 0.61
```
nina: KV hit rate drop is worrying but avg batch size halving smells like scheduler heuristic change. what did the merge change?
maya: the PR switched the batching window to a reshuffle-first policy and tweaked the "prefer_small_batches" heuristic. also changed kernel selector to prefer memcopy-safe path for certain seqlen buckets.
rahul: CI had a perf-check fail on that PR — deploy-bot posted it earlier: 
deploy-bot: PERF-CHECK(rt/batcher): tokens/sec delta -24% (threshold -10%) — https://ci.redwood/runs/pm-9832
liam: can we bisect to the specific commit quickly? rollback seems reasonable if it's a rollout blocker.
eva: started a quick bisect on canary pool now. running binary rollback + perf probe. will post numbers in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
ops-bot: Incident INC-4521 created for continuous-batcher token/sec regression — assigning eng-runtime.
(nina uploads a tiny trace snippet)
nina: propagated traces show more frequent small-batch enqueues, more wakeups and a kernel selection path that triggers an extra memcpy on the hot path. snippet: 
```
# simplified trace
enqueue->coalesce (2.3 items avg) -> kernel_selector: chose fallback_memcopy_path -> launch -> gpu memcpy -> exec
previously: enqueue->coalesce (4.1 items) -> kernel_fast_path -> exec
```
liam: that extra memcpy would explain both token/sec and p95. is fallback being chosen because of an incorrect seq_len classification after reshuffle?
maya: yep, the reshuffle changed how we compute effective_seqlen for coalescing. boundary moved so a bunch of requests now hit the "large-seq" kernel.
rahul: can you run a targeted unit to flip the pref_small_batches flag back and rerun perf-check? if that recovers, we can hotfix without full revert.
eva: test run (canary) toggled prefer_small_batches=false -> tokens/sec 118k (close to baseline), p95 queueing 260ms. repeating twice, stable.
liam: good signal. let's prepare a rollback/hotfix PR to restore previous window heuristic and adjust seqlen thresholds for kernel selector. also add a CI perf test that exercises small batches.
maya: creating #hotfix-pr now. will include: revert reshuffle ordering + bump seqlen threshold + add regression test.
deploy-bot: HOTFIX-PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/4876 (tag: rollback-reshuffle)
ops-bot: Rolling hold applied to rollout channel 'rt-scheduler' until hotfix lands.
rahul: one more ask — add telemetry for kernel-path-chosen in prod (counts per minute) so we can detect this faster next time.
nina: agreed. adding short-term metric and alert (ctb.kernel_fallback_rate > 5%).
eva: hotfix PR merged to canary. canary perf-check: tokens/sec back to 121k, KV hitrate returned to ~0.80, avg batch size 4.0.
maya: merging hotfix to main and scheduling staged rollout with slow ramp. thanks all. :tada:
liam: postmortem notes: root cause = scheduling window reorder + seq_len boundary change -> more small batches -> kernel selector fallback to memcpy path -> throughput drop. action items: revert/shim, add perf CI, telemetry, and add kernel selector unit that simulates coalesced seqlen distributions.
ops-bot: INC-4521 status: resolved (monitoring).
maya: closing thread — will paste postmortem doc link when ready.
